title: Madagascar Healthshed Clinic Data Curation Manual
text:
0.1 Context
This Quarto Manual is the human-facing source of truth for constructing and operating the Madagascar Healthshed Clinic Data pipeline. Its emit profile materializes reviewed configuration and command-line tools. Scientific work is then run explicitly through the generated container runner and targets graph.
In MDG, our research has divvied up the geographical land into “healthsheds.” Healthsheds conceptually represent a catchment area in which nearby residents are expected, under normal circumstances, to attend a central clinic for their healthcare. In doing so, we can ask interesting questions about health as it pertains to an individual’s residential healthshed, and investigate what confounds and other variables influence health outcomes. Importantly, we are also able to use the healthsheds for geospatial data analysis questions, such as by aggregating ERA5 satellite data to each healthshed, and seeing if environmental exposures to heat, precipitation, etc., contribute to health outcomes.
We receive this data from the Ministry of Health in Madagascar, monthly, in the form of database dumps onto Google Drive. Notably, we believe that, being in small, rural clinics, the clinicians are not using very sophisticated EMR. As a result, we have to make the following important assumptions:

0.2 Prior Work & Plan
This project has been ongoing for several years, with several hands having been involved in data management. Contact persons worth keeping in mind:

Chris Golden (PI, present)
G. DeNicola (Post Doc, present)
Marissa Childs (Post Doc, 2024(?))
Tinashe M. Tapera (RSE, present)


Human decision required: confirm the project participants, their roles, and the accountable data steward before source data is staged or inspected.

In general, there are 2 major “blocks” of data: pre-DHIS2, and post.
Pre-implementation of DHSI2, the data were processed ad-hoc and within their means, and post, the introduction of DHIS2 standards made manual fixes and adjustments far less prevalent. In our reproduction of the pipeline, we expect the same truth to hold in implementation. We will keep obvious manual fixes and patches as they are in the pre-DHIS2 data, as there is little we can do to confidently improve on spaghetti code without a comparable true expected outcome to test against. Post DHIS2, we will improve code where necessary to communicate more clearly, or speed up a laborious task.

title: 2  Data Curation Manual
text:
This manual walks the reader through a declarative reproduction of the MDGHealthshedClinicData Prospector.
The manual should:

declaratively create a robust, reproducible computational environment;
safely and declaratively stage input data;
process the data transparently and elegantly;
version and distribute the data to the Frontier.

The Manual separates three operations:

an authoring render produces human-readable documentation;
an emission render synchronizes reviewed scripts and configuration;
the emitted container runner executes R and the targets pipeline.

No render is permitted to inspect or transform protected source data.

# Madagascar Healthshed Clinic Data

This repository contains the executable curation Manual for the Madagascar
Healthshed Clinic Data pipeline. The Manual owns generated configuration and
command-line entry points; scientific execution occurs explicitly through a
Singularity container and a targets graph.

## Current status

Infrastructure and an input-inventory target are scaffolded. Source selection,
schema interpretation, pre-/post-DHIS2 reconciliation, missing-value rules,
disclosure controls, and release design remain documented human decisions.

No protected data is rendered into the Manual or committed to this repository.

## Render the Manual

```sh
scripts/render-isolated --profile authoring
scripts/render-isolated --profile emit
```

The authoring profile updates the rendered Manual. The emit profile also
synchronizes generated scripts and configuration from reviewed `.qmd` source.

## Build and operate the environment

Follow the rendered Infrastructure pages in `docs/infrastructure/`. After the
runtime image and frozen R library exist:

```sh
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec uvr run scripts/run-pipeline.R
```

With no subcommand, the container runner opens a shell in the repository.
Commands require the explicit `exec` subcommand.

title: 3  Render In Isolation
text:
Use scripts/render-isolated from the repository root. It renders a private, data-free staging copy so concurrent jobs do not share Quarto’s mutable cache. Only a successful site and files recorded by quarto-emit are promoted back.






Important Prerequisite: Confirm The Render Boundary



The host needs bash, rsync, mktemp, and quarto. Do not run two publishing renders against the same checkout simultaneously because both would promote to the same docs/ directory.








Tip Procedure: Emit The Isolated Render Wrapper



#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

script_dir=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
project_dir=$(CDPATH= cd -- "${script_dir}/.." && pwd)
stage_dir=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/quarto-render.XXXXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf -- "$stage_dir"' EXIT

export XDG_CACHE_HOME="${stage_dir}/xdg-cache"
export XDG_DATA_HOME="${stage_dir}/xdg-data"
export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="${stage_dir}/xdg-runtime"
mkdir -p "$XDG_CACHE_HOME" "$XDG_DATA_HOME" "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR"

# The Manual does not consume protected data or mutable runtime state.
rsync -a \
  --exclude '.git' \
  --exclude '.jj' \
  --exclude '.quarto' \
  --exclude '.spack-env' \
  --exclude '.uvr' \
  --exclude '_targets' \
  --exclude 'artifacts' \
  --exclude 'data' \
  --exclude 'docs' \
  --exclude 'notebooks/.quarto' \
  --exclude 'notebooks/_site' \
  --exclude 'notebooks/site_libs' \
  --exclude 'notebooks/*labbook' \
  "$project_dir/" "$stage_dir/project/"

(
  cd "$stage_dir/project"
  quarto render notebooks "$@"
)

emit_manifest="$stage_dir/project/.quarto/quarto-emit-manifest.tsv"
stage_project=$(realpath -e "$stage_dir/project")
if [[ -f "$emit_manifest" ]]; then
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r emitted_path source_page; do
    [[ -n "$emitted_path" && -n "$source_page" ]] || continue
    case "$source_page" in
      "$stage_project"/notebooks/*) ;;
      *) echo "Refusing emit source outside notebooks: $source_page" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
    staged_file=$(realpath -e "$(dirname "$source_page")/$emitted_path") || {
      echo "Generated file is missing: $emitted_path" >&2
      exit 1
    }
    case "$staged_file" in
      "$stage_project"/*) ;;
      *) echo "Refusing emit target outside staged project: $staged_file" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
    destination="$project_dir/${staged_file#"$stage_project"/}"
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$destination")"
    rsync -a "$staged_file" "$destination"
  done < "$emit_manifest"
fi

rsync -a --delete "$stage_dir/project/docs/" "$project_dir/docs/"


Use the default profile for documentation and the explicit profile for file generation:
scripts/render-isolated --profile authoring
scripts/render-isolated --profile emit






Warning Check: Verify The Wrapper



bash -n scripts/render-isolated
scripts/render-isolated --profile authoring --no-execute

title: 4  Project Contract
text:
The existing project uses data/raw, data/interim, and data/processed. This Manual preserves those names:

data/raw is the immutable staged-input boundary;
data/interim contains disposable derived state;

notebooks owns the Manual and pipeline declarations;

title: 8  Declare the Native Runtime
text:
spack.yaml declares the native runtime. R 4.5.1 is retained from the existing environment. Neovim is retained deliberately as the interactive IDE for pipeline development. The scientific workflow itself remains command-line-driven.
The x86_64_v3 baseline avoids tying the image to the build node. The system libraries follow the exemplar’s R, Quarto, targets, and graphics build baseline; project-specific additions require evidence from reviewed code.
The native layer includes both FlexiBLAS, which Spack’s R installation uses, and OpenBLAS. The latter is an explicit runtime requirement because binary R packages resolved by uvr can link directly to the libopenblas.so.0 SONAME instead of going through R’s FlexiBLAS interface. Declaring OpenBLAS as a root spec ensures that its shared libraries are linked into the final Spack view.






Important Prerequisite: Confirm The Runtime Policy



Before building, review the R, Neovim, Rocky Linux, Spack, and CPU target versions below. None of these choices are inferred from protected data.








Tip Procedure: Emit The Runtime Declaration



spack:
  specs:
  - r@4.5.1
  - libxml2
  - icu4c
  - libx11
  - git
  - curl
  - openssl
  - libgit2
  - cmake
  - gmake
  - freetype
  - libjpeg-turbo
  - libpng
  - libtiff
  - libwebp
  - fontconfig
  - fribidi
  - harfbuzz
  - libuv
  - glpk
  - flexiblas
  - openblas
  view: true
  concretizer:
    unify: true
  packages:
    all:
      require:
      - target=x86_64_v3
  config:
    template_dirs:
    - $env/containers/templates
    - $spack/share/spack/templates
  container:
    format: singularity
    images:
      os: rockylinux:9
      spack: 1.2.0
    template: MDGHealthshedClinicData.def.j2
    os_packages:
      final:
      - ca-certificates
      - findutils
      - gzip
      - tar
      - which
      - gcc
      - gcc-c++
      - make








Warning Check: Verify The Declaration



rg -n 'r@4.5.1|neovim|flexiblas|openblas|target=x86_64_v3|rockylinux:9' spack.yaml

title: 9  Customize and Build the Runtime
text:
The Jinja extension adds uvr, Quarto, ARF, and the Spack view to Spack’s generated Singularity recipe. ARF is installed from its pinned, checksummed Linux Rust-binary release. The image supplies R and its native runtime dependencies; uvr retains ownership of project-library and cache resolution at runtime.
The extension configures only image-owned executable, header, metadata, and shared-library search paths. It does not set UVR_LIBRARY, UVR_CACHE_DIR, R_LIBS_USER, or R_LIBS: those paths are project state, so uvr resolves them after the repository is mounted at /work.
ARF dynamically loads R’s C API rather than merely starting an R subprocess. The template therefore preserves the environment emitted by Spack’s parent template, including the R library directory contributed by environment activation. The ARF smoke test starts a headless R session under --cleanenv- equivalent image conditions, which catches a missing libR.so or one of its transitive native libraries.
The container also owns a UTF-8 locale invariant: LANG and LC_ALL are set to C.UTF-8 in the image environment. The runner uses --cleanenv, which otherwise leaves R in the ASCII C locale. In that locale, R’s list.files() turns a valid combining-accent filename byte sequence into literal text such as <cc><81>, creating a path that cannot exist. Setting the invariant in the image makes filename enumeration deterministic and independent of the host login locale. The build-time %test runs before Singularity applies this image environment, so the post-build verification below is the check that the invariant is actually active at runtime.






Important Prerequisite: Confirm The Builder And Container Runtime



command -v singularity
test -r artifacts/containers/spack-builder.sif









Tip Procedure: Emit The Final-Image Extension



{% extends "container/singularity.def" %}

{% block build_stage %}
{{ super() }}
  set -euo pipefail
  UVR_VERSION=0.4.6
  QUARTO_VERSION=1.9.38
  ARF_VERSION=0.5.2
  ARF_ARCHIVE=arf-console-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz
  ARF_SHA256=64bb48569e79b91d0b258445173a78b5ad74e9274e8fd17b524c64531405b987
  curl --fail --location --show-error --output /tmp/uvr.tar.gz \
    "https://github.com/nbafrank/uvr/releases/download/v${UVR_VERSION}/uvr-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"
  mkdir -p /opt/uvr/bin
  tar -xzf /tmp/uvr.tar.gz -C /opt/uvr/bin
  rm -f /tmp/uvr.tar.gz
  /opt/uvr/bin/uvr --version | grep -Fx "uvr ${UVR_VERSION}"
  curl --fail --location --show-error --output /tmp/quarto.tar.gz \
    "https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/download/v${QUARTO_VERSION}/quarto-${QUARTO_VERSION}-linux-amd64.tar.gz"
  mkdir -p /opt/quarto
  tar -xzf /tmp/quarto.tar.gz -C /opt/quarto --strip-components=1
  rm -f /tmp/quarto.tar.gz
  /opt/quarto/bin/quarto --version | grep -Fx "${QUARTO_VERSION}"
  curl --fail --location --show-error --output "/tmp/${ARF_ARCHIVE}" \
    "https://github.com/eitsupi/arf/releases/download/v${ARF_VERSION}/${ARF_ARCHIVE}"
  printf '%s  %s\n' "${ARF_SHA256}" "/tmp/${ARF_ARCHIVE}" | sha256sum --check --strict
  mkdir -p /tmp/arf /opt/arf/bin
  tar -xJf "/tmp/${ARF_ARCHIVE}" -C /tmp/arf
  install -m 0755 "/tmp/arf/${ARF_ARCHIVE%.tar.xz}/arf" /opt/arf/bin/arf
  /opt/arf/bin/arf --version | grep -Fx "arf ${ARF_VERSION}"
{% endblock %}

{% block final_stage %}
{{ super() }}
%files from build
  /opt/uvr /opt/uvr
  /opt/quarto /opt/quarto
  /opt/arf /opt/arf
  /opt/spack-environment/spack.lock /opt/spack-environment/spack.lock
%post
  set -eu
  ln -sf /opt/uvr/bin/uvr /usr/local/bin/uvr
  ln -sf /opt/quarto/bin/quarto /usr/local/bin/quarto
  ln -sf /opt/arf/bin/arf /usr/local/bin/arf
  cat >> "$SINGULARITY_ENVIRONMENT" <<'EOF'
unset R_HOME
export LANG=C.UTF-8
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
export SPACK_VIEW=/opt/views/view
export PATH="/usr/local/bin:/opt/views/view/bin:${PATH}"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/views/view/lib/pkgconfig:/opt/views/view/lib64/pkgconfig:/opt/views/view/share/pkgconfig:${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:-}"
export CPATH="/opt/views/view/include:${CPATH:-}"
export LIBRARY_PATH="/opt/views/view/lib:/opt/views/view/lib64:${LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/opt/views/view/lib:/opt/views/view/lib64:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
EOF
%test
  set -eu
  command -v R
  command -v Rscript
  command -v uvr
  command -v quarto
  command -v arf
  R --version
  uvr --version
  quarto --version | grep -Fx "1.9.38"
  arf --version | grep -Fx "arf 0.5.2"
  LANG=C.UTF-8 LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 Rscript --vanilla -e 'quit(status = if (l10n_info()[["UTF-8"]]) 0 else 1)'
  test -r /opt/views/view/lib/libopenblas.so.0
  r_home=$(R RHOME)
  test -r "${r_home}/lib/libR.so"
  test -r /opt/spack-environment/spack.lock
  test ! -e /opt/spack/bin/spack
{% endblock %}

title: 10  Lock and Synchronize R Packages
text:
uvr.toml declares direct R requirements and uvr.lock records their resolved versions. The SIF supplies the stable R ABI and the uvr executable. At runtime, uvr owns its project library, cache, R-version resolution, and activation files; the container and runner do not override them.
Only packages required by the scaffold are declared now. Add readers, transformers, validators, and release tooling only after the corresponding Manual decisions and code exist.






Important Prerequisite: Confirm The Direct Dependencies



Review the dependency list below. A dependency belongs here only when Manual or pipeline code imports it.








Tip Procedure: Emit The R Package Declaration



[project]
name = "prospectorMDGHealthshedClinicData"
r_version = "4.5.1"

[dependencies]
parsermd = "*"
skimr = "*"
duckdb = "*"
duckplyr = "*"
here = "*"
targets = "*"
tarchetypes = "*"








Tip Procedure: Resolve And Synchronize In The Container



scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec uvr lock
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec uvr sync
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec uvr sync --frozen
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec uvr activate --write-shim
Commit uvr.lock only after successful resolution through the built runtime. Use uvr r pin only when an additional exact .r-version pin is intentional; do not generate that optional file outside uvr.
Run scripts through uvr run. For an interactive session, enter the container shell and source .uvr/activate; that shim asks uvr to resolve the current project environment instead of storing hard-coded paths.








Warning Check: Verify The R Environment Contract



test -f uvr.toml
rg -n '^r_version = "4.5.1"|^targets =|^tarchetypes =' uvr.toml
test -f uvr.lock
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec uvr sync --frozen
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec Rscript -e 'library(targets)'

title: 11  Run the Project Environment
text:
The runner is the only place that selects the image, cleans the host environment, and binds writable project state. Interactive shells, explicit command execution, and Slurm all consume this same boundary.






Important Prerequisite: Confirm The Runtime Image



Build the image from the preceding pages or set MDG_HEALTHSHED_CLINIC_DATA_IMAGE in containers/runtime/local.env.









Tip Procedure: Emit The Environment Runner



#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

project_dir=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage:
  mdg-healthshed-clinic-data [shell [SHELL_OPTION...]]
  mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec COMMAND [ARG...]

With no arguments, open a shell in /work. Commands must use the explicit
`exec` subcommand.
EOF
}

action=${1:-shell}
if (( $# > 0 )); then
  shift
fi

case "${action}" in
  shell) ;;
  exec)
    if (( $# == 0 )); then
      echo "The exec subcommand requires a command." >&2
      usage >&2
      exit 64
    fi
    ;;
  -h|--help)
    usage
    exit 0
    ;;
  *)
    echo "Unknown subcommand: ${action}" >&2
    usage >&2
    exit 64
    ;;
esac

local_env="${project_dir}/containers/runtime/local.env"
if [[ -f "${local_env}" ]]; then
  set -a
  source "${local_env}"
  set +a
fi

runtime=${CONTAINER_RUNTIME:-apptainer}
if ! command -v "${runtime}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  runtime=singularity
fi
command -v "${runtime}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
  echo "Neither apptainer nor singularity is available." >&2
  exit 127
}

image=${MDG_HEALTHSHED_CLINIC_DATA_IMAGE:-"${project_dir}/artifacts/containers/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data.sif"}
test -r "${image}" || {
  echo "Container image not readable: ${image}" >&2
  echo "Build it from the Infrastructure pages or set MDG_HEALTHSHED_CLINIC_DATA_IMAGE." >&2
  exit 1
}

runtime_options=(
  --cleanenv
  --bind "${project_dir}:/work"
  --pwd /work
)

case "${action}" in
  shell)
    exec "${runtime}" shell "${runtime_options[@]}" "$@" "${image}"
    ;;
  exec)
    exec "${runtime}" exec "${runtime_options[@]}" "${image}" "$@"
    ;;
esac

  slurm/launch/launch_container.sbatch

pipeline_raw_input_files_paths <- {

  if (!length(input_paths)) {

}

title: 14  Curate the Healthshed Clinic Data
text:
This is the future source of the cleaning target declarations. It is not yet registered in _targets.R because inspecting filenames does not justify guessing a schema or transformation.






Important Prerequisite: Approve The Curation Contract



The source-inspection page must first record the source schema, record grain, stable keys, pre-/post-DHIS2 boundary, missing-value semantics, validation rules, and disclosure controls.








Tip Procedure: Prep Raw RMA_DEPSI Files



In this first section of the script, we take raw files and prepare them by aggregating them into a single CSV, one row per clinic-year-month, and one column per health outcome-age-sex.
Applies only to 2020-2022 data.
library(targets)
library(readr)
library(openxlsx)
library(data.table)
library(cli)

tar_load(pipeline_raw_input_files_paths)
We have a variable number of missing values in our first rows of data, so we’ll need to ensure they don’t get read as logical NAs. To prevent this, the following wraps our CSV reader:
read_csv_nonlogical <- function(filepath){

  spec <- spec_csv(filepath) 

  spec$cols %>% 
    purrr::map(function(x){
      if("collector_logical" %in% class(x)){return(col_number())
      } else{return(x)}
    }) -> spec$cols
  
  read_csv(filepath, 
    col_types = spec) %>% 
    return
  
}
process_csv_safely <- function(csv_path, drop_cols = c("organisationunitcode", "orgnaisationunitdescription")) {
  stopifnot(length(csv_path) == 1L, file.exists(csv_path))
  
  cli_alert_info(paste("Working on:", csv_path))
  
  # Read file with type-safe reader
  temp_df <- read_csv_nonlogical(csv_path)
  
  # Drop the extra columns if they exist
  temp_df <- temp_df %>%
    select(-any_of(drop_cols))
  
  # Optional: check for duplicate records
  dups <- temp_df %>%
    filter(duplicated(select(., organisationunitid, periodname)))
  
  cli_alert_info(paste("Successfully created dataframe for", csv_path, "with shape", nrow(temp_df), "x", ncol(temp_df)))
  cli_alert_info(paste("Number of duplicate clinic-month-year records:", nrow(dups)))
  
  # Convert all description fields, if any, to character.
  temp_df |>
    mutate(
      across(
        contains("description", ignore.case = TRUE),
        as.character
      )
    )
}
process_csv_safely() intentionally accepts exactly one path and never holds other input tables in memory. _targets.R selects the RMA_W3_FULL paths and defines a dynamic map() branch for each path outside this notebook. That makes each CSV independently schedulable and prevents a single worker from holding every parsed table before aggregation. Dynamic branching enables parallel execution; the approved Slurm allocation and selected targets backend determine how many branches run concurrently.

Future checks must test the documented invariants and compare observed exceptions with reviewer-approved expectations. “The code ran” is not sufficient evidence of correct curation.

16  Execute the Pipeline
text:
The graph inventories staged paths and dynamically branches the approved W3 CSV preparation work. Branching is declared here rather than in the notebook: the notebook defines one-file transformation logic, while this graph defines dependencies and the scheduler can distribute independent branches.






Important Prerequisite: Confirm The Execution Boundary



The runtime image and frozen R package library must exist. Approved inputs must be staged under data/raw. Rendering the Manual is not pipeline execution.









Tip Procedure: Emit The Targets Graph



library(targets)
library(tarchetypes)

tar_option_set(
  packages = c("here", "readr", "cli", "glue", "purrr", "stringr", "dplyr")
)

list(
  tarchetypes::tar_tangle(
    "notebooks/pipeline/16_page-stage-inputs.qmd"
  ),
  tarchetypes::tar_tangle(
    "notebooks/pipeline/18_page-prep-w3.qmd"
  ),
  tar_target(
    clinic_raw_data_RMA_W3_csv_path,
    pipeline_raw_input_files_paths %>%
      str_subset("RMA_W3_FULL")
  ),
  tar_target(
    clinic_raw_data_RMA_W3_df,
    process_csv_safely(clinic_raw_data_RMA_W3_csv_path),
    pattern = map(clinic_raw_data_RMA_W3_csv_path)
  )
)









Tip Procedure: Emit The Pipeline Entry Point



#!/usr/bin/env Rscript

script_arg <- grep("^--file=", commandArgs(trailingOnly = FALSE), value = TRUE)
script_path <- if (length(script_arg)) sub("^--file=", "", script_arg[[1]]) else ""
if (!nzchar(script_path)) {
  stop("Could not determine the pipeline runner path.")
}

repository_root <- normalizePath(
  file.path(dirname(script_path), ".."),
  mustWork = TRUE
)
setwd(repository_root)
targets::tar_make()
